companyDescription: Memory & storage leader · HBM4 dominant AI memory supplier · New Ford long-term supply agreement · 16 take-or-pay SCAs worth $100B+ · Q4 FY26 guide $50B
priceNote: Fell 4.71% Jul 7 (premarket Jul 8 indicated further down near $902) in a sector-wide semiconductor de-rating — Samsung's blowout Q2 profit was read as 'AI memory euphoria priced in,' Morgan Stanley cut semi exposure, and DeepSeek's in-house AI chip report added to the selling. Now ~25% off the Jun 25 ATH of $1,255, despite signing a new long-term supply deal with Ford the same week.
summary: Micron has fallen roughly 25% from its Jun 25 all-time high of $1,255 as a sector-wide AI-hardware de-rating swept through chip stocks — triggered by Samsung's 19x profit jump being read as a 'sell-the-news' peak signal, Morgan Stanley recommending reduced semiconductor exposure, and a Reuters report on DeepSeek's in-house AI chip. Michael Burry's disclosed short against Micron added to the bearish narrative. None of this reflects a Micron-specific problem: the company just signed a new long-term supply agreement with Ford (one of 16 SCAs worth $100B+ in customer commitments, ~40% of total sales), HBM4 remains sold out through 2027, and Wall Street targets have kept climbing (BofA to $1,500, UBS $1,625). Q4 FY2026 earnings (~Sep 22-23) is the next catalyst.

catalysts.name: Sector-Wide AI-Chip De-Rating
catalysts.description: Jul 6-8, 2026: Samsung's record Q2 profit was read as 'AI memory euphoria priced in,' Morgan Stanley cut semiconductor weightings, and a Reuters report on DeepSeek's proprietary AI chip added to the selling. MU -4.71% Jul 7, PHLX Semiconductor Index -4.7%, Micron ~25% off its Jun 25 ATH. Not a Micron-specific issue — a valuation reset after a >250% YTD run.

catalysts.name: New Ford Motor Long-Term Supply Agreement
catalysts.description: Micron signed a new long-term supply agreement with Ford for next-generation vehicle memory and storage — one of 16 strategic customer agreements (SCAs) that together secure roughly $100B in revenue, about 40% of total sales, insulating Micron from the typical memory boom-bust cycle.

catalysts.name: Q4 FY2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Estimated Sep 22-23, 2026 (unconfirmed). Company guided $50B ± $1B revenue and $31 ± $1 non-GAAP EPS. Beat bar is $51B+ revenue or $32+ EPS — the next major re-rating event after the sector selloff.

catalysts.name: HBM4 Revenue Ramp — Vera Rubin Supply
catalysts.description: Micron is the primary HBM4 supplier for NVIDIA's Vera Rubin GPUs, shipping now. Fully booked through 2027 — a structural demand floor that the sector selloff hasn't changed.

risks: Sector-wide de-rating risk: Samsung and SK Hynix also fell sharply (up to 5.2%) — if this is the start of a broader AI-valuation unwind rather than a one-week reset, Micron falls with the group regardless of its own fundamentals
Michael Burry's disclosed short position against Micron adds a visible bearish voice to the narrative, even as bulls (Ross Gerber, several sell-side analysts) defend the fundamentals
DeepSeek reportedly developing its own AI inference chip — a long-term risk to AI-hardware demand assumptions across the memory/GPU supply chain if it ships and scales
Oversupply shock 2027-2028 — Micron ($27B+ capex), Samsung and SK Hynix are all building simultaneously; synchronized capacity could eventually crash ASPs
China export controls — BIS enforcement and the Match Act create geopolitical tail risk for a company with significant China exposure
Peak margin trajectory — Micron's own Q4 guidance notes 'meaningful moderation in rate of price increases'

estimateDates.note: Revenue $50B ± $1B / EPS $31 ± $1 — true beat bar is $51B+ or $32+ EPS
2026 HBM supply fully sold out; orders extending into 2028

analystTargets.note: Kept target through the selloff, calls the dip a buying opportunity
Cited better-than-expected memory pricing + tight supply

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed on hold at 3.50-3.75%; next FOMC Jul 28-29. Memory demand is driven primarily by hyperscaler AI capex, which is structural and contracted — partially insulated from near-term rate moves.
macroRisk.inflationNote: June CPI (Jul 14) is the next checkpoint. DRAM/NAND pricing is driven by supply/demand dynamics rather than inflation directly, but a hot CPI print would add to the broader tech/semi risk-off tone currently pressuring MU.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: The Jul 6-8 selloff is a sector-wide AI-hardware valuation reset (Samsung, SK Hynix, Intel, AMD all fell alongside Micron), not a demand problem — AI memory demand remains structural and contracted via 16 take-or-pay SCAs.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — fundamental demand is strong and contracted (HBM4 sold out through 2027, new Ford SCA), but the current sector-wide de-rating plus 2027-2028 oversupply and geopolitical chip-restriction risk are real near/medium-term overhangs.

entryStrategy.verdict: Buy the sector-wide AI-hardware de-rating — Micron's own fundamentals (new Ford SCA, HBM4 sold out through 2027, Q3 blowout) haven't changed; this is a valuation reset, not a demand break. Q4 earnings (~Sep 22) is the next re-rating event.

catalystSpot.preRunup: MU typically rallies 8-15% in the 2-4 weeks before earnings on AI demand data points (TSMC capacity reports, hyperscaler capex signals). The current post-selloff consolidation near $900-940 is the pre-Q4 entry window.

postWin.note: Q3 FY2026 (Jun 25): +14.55% AH on a blowout beat. Prior cycle: Q3 FY2025 beat +20% AH. MU has historically been one of the biggest earnings movers in semiconductors on large beats.

postLose.note: Q2 FY2026 (Mar 2026): beat but -4%+ on guidance concerns. Any Q4 revenue miss vs. the $50B guide, on top of the current sector caution, would risk a sharper de-rating than usual.

spotSizing.reason: High conviction: HBM4 fully booked 2026-2027, 16 take-or-pay SCAs including the new Ford deal, and Wall Street targets imply 60-73% upside from the post-selloff price. Size 6% as a Core Holding; the sector-wide selloff is a better entry, not a worse one, provided the demand thesis holds.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below the pre-earnings/50-day base = thesis changing on China restrictions, Samsung HBM4 qualification, or a deeper AI-valuation unwind

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Q4 revenue comes in below $49B or guidance is cut below $50B for Q1 FY2027, exit within 2 sessions

comparableCases.event: Q3 FY2026 blowout earnings — revenue quadrupled YoY
comparableCases.note: Q3 FY2026 on Jun 25: $41.5B revenue vs $35.7B estimate (+16.2%), EPS $25.11 vs $20.49 (+22.6%). Stock +14.55% AH — established the new earnings baseline that the current sector selloff has temporarily overshadowed.

Samsung's blowout Q2 profit (19x jump) was read as 'AI memory euphoria fully priced in,' triggering a broad chip-sector selloff that took Micron down ~25% from its Jun 25 ATH despite no negative Micron-specific news — a valuation reset driven by sentiment, not fundamentals.
